first.rationale: The situation shows simultaneous declines in both activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). While competitive pricing pressure exists, the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not short-term acquisition. Memory 31 and 86 are well-established evidence that onboarding simplification drives measurable improvements in activation and completion. Memory 91 reinforces that activation messaging is an effective lever. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding directly addresses the measurable drop in completion rates and has proven durable lift in the archived record. This is lower-risk than promotional_pricing (which could trigger a race-to-bottom with the competitor) and more targeted than referral_incentive (which works best in established cohorts, not relevant to current activation decline). Enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to the SMB-driven activation problem. Verifying memories 31 and 86 will confirm whether the original field-reduction approach and scope remain applicable given day-76 context.

final.rationale: Archive confirmation shows memory_31 (signup simplification) lifted SMB activation +9% and qualified revenue +4% with only -1% retention risk, and memory_86 (shortened onboarding) achieved +13% completion lift and +3% retention gain. Current situation shows onboarding completion down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ. Both archived experiments demonstrate durable, retention-safe improvements to the exact metrics now declining. Simplify_onboarding is the highest-confidence play: it addresses measurable declines in completion and activation simultaneously, it has proven retention benefits (not erosion), and it aligns with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Promotional_pricing would be reactive to competitor pressure and risks margin; referral_incentive targets established cohorts, not the activation problem; enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to SMB activation. A standard_experiment scope is appropriate for testing field-reduction and flow streamlining on SMB signup/onboarding, consistent with the proven SMB-specific effects in memory_31.
